analysis:
Examined ClusterService.swift. Base units 4 and 5 (lines 912-1512) contain unchanged supervision, approval and update logic. Only base line 164, the init signature, changed. Head unit 6 (lines 1-471) shows the visible changes: a new private `environment: [String: String]?` property (head 80-81) and an `init` parameter defaulting to nil (head 166-167, 173). It is internal-only; the public `convenience init(settings:)` is unchanged, so the public API gains no caller-controlled environment.

The patch excerpt is truncated. It indicates `supervise` now sets `process.environment = Self.partEnvironment(environment ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment, serviceDirectory: store.paths.directory)` (head ~1426) and that `removeEndedApproval` was modified (head ~1446-1461). Neither the head text for those ranges nor the `partEnvironment` implementation was supplied, so I could not verify what it passes, strips or adds.

Open questions for the next pass:
(1) Does `partEnvironment` keep or force DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_TTL_SECONDS and DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_DISK_GB? That bears on T-041 and SEC-035. Previously the part inherited the service environment (Process.environment nil).
(2) Does it add anything that exposes the service directory or private paths, or could it allow environment injection (DYLD_*, proxy or coordinator URL variables) into the worker or provider part that runs with provider credentials (A-008, TB-003)?
(3) What changed in `removeEndedApproval`? It writes the setup without the cluster approval, which is relevant to the approval and attestation flow (TB-011, T-053).

No concrete regression is established from the visible lines, so I report none. The truncated hunks leave a security-relevant uncertainty.
